overview: The Medford School Committee approved a proclamation aiming to make Medford hunger-free by 2028, heard extensive advocacy from high school student workers seeking minimum wage increases, reviewed district operations including the middle school lottery and kindergarten registration, and received a presentation on a draft three-year strategic plan.

items.title: Approval of Minutes and Financial Reports
items.summary: The committee approved the minutes of January 13, 2020, along with bills, payrolls, and fund transfers, following a brief review of employee reimbursement procedures.

items.title: Proclamation to Make Medford Hunger-Free
items.summary: The committee approved a proclamation setting a goal to eliminate food insecurity in Medford by January 1, 2028, and creating an advisory committee to make specific implementation recommendations.

items.title: Resolution and Public Comment on Student Minimum Wage
items.summary: The committee approved a resolution to schedule a Committee of the Whole meeting and direct the administration to identify all positions paid below minimum wage after several student workers from the after-school program advocated for fair compensation and back pay.

items.title: Coronavirus Health Update
items.summary: Health Services Supervisor Toni Wray provided an informational update regarding state and federal guidance on the novel coronavirus and current local monitoring efforts.

items.title: Report of the Secretary
items.summary: Secretary Van der Kloot shared documentation regarding interpretation service invoices, odor remediation at Curtis-Tufts, and newly arrived seventh-grade civics textbooks.

items.title: Report of the Superintendent
items.summary: Superintendent Edouard-Vincent announced the launch of the new district website and highlighted numerous student academic, arts, and athletic achievements.

items.title: Donations and DECA Field Trip Approvals
items.summary: The committee approved a $5,000 Encore Boston community fund donation to CCSR, an overnight field trip for the DECA state competition, an equipment donation from Nardone Electric for vocational electrical students, and a $500 ExxonMobil grant.

items.title: Report on Personnel Activity
items.summary: Assistant Superintendent Patterson presented a report detailing 185 new hires, 38 departures, and 61 extended leaves across the district since July 2019.

items.title: Report on 2020 Middle School Lottery
items.summary: The committee received the timeline and plan for the second annual middle school lottery, approved a motion requesting demographic data breakdowns, directed the administration to issue an explanatory communication to fifth-grade families by February 14, and referred future lottery review to subcommittee.

items.title: Building Bridges to Kindergarten
items.summary: Assistant Superintendent Caldwell reported on upcoming kindergarten registration and orientation events, and the committee voted to refer kindergarten onboarding practices to the Communications subcommittee for review by September 30, 2020.

items.title: Draft Strategic Plan Presentation
items.summary: Administrators presented the district's draft 2020–2023 strategic plan centered on the core values of Achievement, Collaboration, Equity, and Support (ACES), and the committee referred the draft to the Strategic Planning subcommittee.

items.title: Meeting Materials and Committee Updates
items.summary: The committee approved motions to add regular member updates to meetings and to publish weekly meeting packets online for the public by Monday afternoons.

items.title: Resolutions on Committee Report Requests and Schedules
items.summary: The committee referred the creation of formal rules for requesting ad hoc reports and establishing an annual schedule of recurring reports to the Rules, Policy, and Equity Subcommittee.

items.title: Resolution on Dyslexia Update Report
items.summary: The committee approved a resolution requesting an administrative update on dyslexia screening and intervention at the February 24 meeting.

items.title: Resolution in Support of the Healthy Youth Act
items.summary: The committee passed a resolution endorsing state legislation (H.410) regarding comprehensive sexual health education in public schools.

items.title: Safety Protocols and Outstanding Reports
items.summary: The committee tabled a discussion on school safety protocols to February 24, referred the status of outstanding reports to the Rules subcommittee, and concluded with a moment of silence for deceased community members.
